title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Handbook (2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

This handbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance cycles, feedback, manager responsibilities, and related people policies. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, engineering managers, and people managers across the company. Use this as the authoritative reference for operational steps, timelines, and templates; procedural checklists live in the linked quickstarts and templates page.

Scope

Covers: role intake and requisition, interview loop design and scorecards, offer and compensation approval, 1st day/30/60/90 onboarding plan, probation and new-hire check-ins, performance review cadence (annual & mid-year), calibration, feedback/one-on-one guidance, promotions and leveling, and offboarding basics. Does not replace legal or finance approvals for offers; see Finance & Legal for final sign-off steps.

Principles

- Candidate experience first: predictable timelines and timely communication.
- Bias reduction: structured scorecards, diverse panels, and standardized rubrics.
- Speed with quality: target times to fill that balance hiring velocity and candidate evaluation.
- Manager empowerment: managers own role definition and hiring decisions; people-ops enablement keeps process compliant and efficient.

Hiring process (end-to-end)

1. Role intake and approval
  - Manager fills Role Intake Form (Jira template or People Ops intake): role description, suggested level, justification, hiring committee, target start date, budget code.
  - People Ops reviews for role alignment, level guidance, and comp band.
  - Approval chain: hiring manager -> people-ops partner -> finance (if above budget threshold) -> VP.
  - SLA: 95% of standard role requests get initial feedback within 3 business days.

2. Requisition posting & sourcing
  - Internal posting policy: roles are posted internally for 3 business days before external searches unless urgent.
  - Sourcing channels: careers site, LinkedIn Recruiter, employee referrals, recruiting partners, campus channels.
  - Time-to-fill KPI: target median = 45 days for engineering roles; track by role family.

3. Interview design & scorecards
  - Mandatory interviewers: recruiter, hiring manager, technical evaluator(s), peer, and (for senior roles) cross-functional partner.
  - Use structured scorecards: competencies (role-specific skills, problem-solving, collaboration, ownership, communication). Each competency: 1-5 rating and required comments.
  - Panel diversity requirement: at least one interviewer from a different team/function where feasible.
  - Interview loop template (recommended):
    1) Recruiter screen (30 min) -- cultural fit, compensation expectation, logistics.
    2) Technical screen (45-60 min) -- coding/system-design/role-specific.
    3) Onsite/loop (4-5 sessions, 45-60 min each) -- scope: deep technical, architecture, product sense, execution examples, leadership/managerial checks.

4. Offer & negotiation
  - Offer approval workflow: recruiter packages offer -> hiring manager signs off -> people-ops verifies comp band and equity -> finance approves high-comp offers (> threshold) -> offer letter generated by people-ops.
  - Offer windows & SLA: aim to present offers within 72 hours of final interview. People-ops tracks offer acceptance rates; target acceptance rate >= 70% for core roles.
  - Template clauses: probation period (if applicable), equity vesting schedule, benefits summary, relocation or remote-work terms.

Onboarding (first 90 days)

Overview
  - Goal: reduce time-to-productivity, create clarity on expectations, and integrate new hires into team culture and systems.
  - Standard 30/60/90 template provided in quickstarts with manager-owned objectives.

Pre-boarding (before first day)
  - People Ops actions: send welcome email, benefits enrollment links, desk/remote equipment order, assign buddy, create IT tickets.
  - Manager actions: send role-specific welcome note, draft 30/60/90 goals, schedule first-week meetings and team lunch.
  - IT actions: ensure accounts provisioned (email, Slack, GitHub, internal tools).

Day 1 checklist (manager + people-ops)
  - Welcome and introductions; team orientation (30-60 min).
  - HR/benefits orientation (people-ops).
  - Workspace & access verification: successful login to email, Slack, GH, CI systems, internal wiki.
  - Buddy assigned and calendar of 1:1s scheduled for first 30 days.

30/60/90 checkpoints
  - 1-week: basic access validated; new hire comfortable with dev environment and key docs.
  - 30-day: initial deliverable completed; manager provides written feedback.
  - 60-day: measurable progress on 30/60/90 objectives; check-in with people-ops on any blockers.
  - 90-day: formal probation review (if probation exists) and confirmation of ongoing employment or extension plan.

Onboarding access matrix (text table)
  - "Tool | Provisioned by | SLA"
  - "Email & SSO | IT | 1 business day"
  - "Slack | IT | 1 business day"
  - "GitHub | Eng Platform | 2 business days"
  - "Dev cluster / GPU access | Eng Infra | 3 business days (request with justification)"

Manager playbook: first 30 days

- Schedule recurring weekly 1:1s (first 90 days weekly recommended).
- Define and agree 30/60/90 goals with measurable signals of success.
- Provide clear onboarding tasks and documentation links.
- Introduce to top 5 stakeholders and cross-functional partners.
- Give early feedback (both reinforcing and corrective) and solicit upward feedback.

Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence
  - Regular: weekly 1:1s between manager and report.
  - Formal reviews: annual performance review (default cadence: late Q4) and optional mid-year review for calibration/change.
  - Goal-setting: use OKR/individual goals aligned to team objectives; update quarterly.

Review process overview
  - Manager writes initial assessment and calibration notes.
  - Peer feedback collected via short forms (anonymous by default).
  - Calibration meeting: managers and people-ops-level lead align ratings and context.
  - People-ops finalizes letter and comp adjustments.

Rating rubric (summary)
  - Exceeds expectations (Top), Meets expectations (Core), Needs improvement (Development area).
  - Each rating should have explicit examples and impact statements.

Promotion & leveling guidance

- Promotion triggers: sustained performance above current level, demonstrated impact across teams, and readiness using leveling rubric.
- Manager responsibilities: prepare promotion packet (summary, examples, peer feedback, proposed new level and comp), discuss with people-ops, submit for calibration.
- SLA: promotions reviewed in the next quarterly calibration cycle; urgent promotions can be routed with VP approval.

Probation & performance improvement

- Probationary period: typically 90 days for new hires (shortened/extended only with people-ops approval).
- Early performance concerns: manager documents specific examples, gives a 30-60 day informal performance plan and frequent 1:1s.
- Formal PIP: when informal coaching is insufficient, manager with people-ops initiates a Performance Improvement Plan with clear objectives, success metrics, and timeline (typically 60 days).

Feedback culture & continuous coaching

- Managers should give feedback in public for reinforcement and private for developmental coaching.
- Use "Situation-Behavior-Impact" (SBI) model for clarity.
- Encourage upward feedback: managers should solicit structured upward feedback quarterly.

Offboarding basics

- Initiation: manager notifies people-ops and IT when offboarding date is set.
- Checklist: revoke access (email/SSO/Slack/GH), collect company assets, conduct exit interview, settle final payroll/benefits with finance.

Important policies & compliance notes

- Employment verification, right-to-work, background checks: required before start for applicable roles and regions.
- Confidentiality & IP agreements: all hires must sign before access to codebase; people-ops ensures signed docs are in file.
- Accommodation & disability requests: people-ops manages confidentially and coordinates reasonable accommodations.

Operational measures & KPIs (people-ops dashboard)

- Time-to-fill (median) by role family -- target: 45 days for engineering, 35 days for non-technical.
- Offer acceptance rate -- target: >= 70% for core product/eng hires.
- New-hire retention 90-day -- target: >= 85%.
- First-week access SLA compliance -- target: 98%.

Templates and artifacts (links)

- Role Intake Form (Jira): link in quickstarts.
- Interview scorecard (Google Form / internal template).
- Offer letter templates (people-ops drive).
- 30/60/90 template and manager onboarding checklist.
- Promotion packet template and PIP template.

Escalation & ownership

- Day-to-day owner for hiring process: assigned recruiter and hiring manager.
- People Ops contact: primary people-ops partner assigned to org.
- Escalation path: recruiter -> people-ops partner -> Head of People Ops -> COO for urgent headcount/case exceptions.

Appendix: quick checklists and decision trees (summary)

- Hiring decision tree: internal candidate? yes -> interview for role fit only; no -> proceed with full loop.
- Offer negotiation quick guide: counteroffer considerations, market comp guidance, approval thresholds.

Document governance

- This handbook is maintained by People Ops (owner). Major updates require reviewer sign-off and notification to all managers. Annual review scheduled in Q1 each year.

Related resources

- See linked quickstarts for forms and step-by-step templates. For legal clauses, consult Finance & Legal. For role-specific onboarding for engineering teams, see Eng Developer Experience quickstarts.
